why: Bible Atlas links Lydia, the seller of purple in Acts 16, to 1:39; the verse names Timna, Lotan's sister. Here Moab means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.

Bible Atlas draws Ezem, Tolad, Bethuel and Baal in Gilead, east of the Jordan, and Rimmon in Syria, but 4:28-33 lists them among Simeon's towns in the Negev, so no dots are drawn for them. Here Moab means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
Here Gad and Manasseh mean the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.

Bible Atlas's Jordan point is near the river's sources in the far north, but 6:78 speaks of the Jordan across from Jericho, so no dot is drawn. Here Benjamin, Manasseh, Asher, Issachar, Naphtali, Gad, Reuben, Zebulun, Simeon and Ephraim mean the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
Bible Atlas draws Ayyah near Gaza, but 7:28 sets it at the edge of Ephraim's land beyond Shechem, so no dot is drawn.
Here Moab means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
Here Benjamin, Ephraim, Manasseh and Levi mean the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
Here Moab and Benjamin mean the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.

In 12:7 Gedor is the town the sons of Jeroham came from, which is linked as a place, not the Benjaminite named Gedor. Here Benjamin, Gad, Manasseh, Simeon, Levi, Ephraim, Issachar, Zebulun, Naphtali and Asher mean the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
Bible Atlas draws this point far up the Nile in Sudan, but Shihor in 13:5 marks Egypt's border with Israel, near the Nile delta or the Brook of Egypt, so no dot is drawn.
Here Canaan means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
Many Christians read the promise of David's offspring in 17:11-14 as pointing to the Messiah, but the verses do not name him; in the chapter they speak of Solomon, who will build the house.

In 18:11-13 the chapter names Edom, the land and its people, not Esau himself; Bible Atlas links Esau because Edom descends from him. Here Moab means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
Bible Atlas puts Mesopotamia at Babylon, but Aram-naharaim in 19:6 is the land of the Arameans in the north, between the Euphrates and the Habor, so no dot is drawn.

In 21:2 ("from Beersheba as far as Dan") Dan is the northern city, which is linked separately as a place, not Jacob's son Dan or his tribe. Here Benjamin and Levi mean the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
Here Manasseh means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
Here Israel, Ephraim, Issachar, Naphtali, Zebulun, Manasseh, Benjamin and Dan mean the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
